newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Oil-rich, cash-poor Azerbaijan sells first T-bills.
newsitem.headline: Oil-rich, cash-poor Azerbaijan sells first T-bills.

text.p: Azerbaijan issued its first Treasury bills on Friday, in a bold step by the oil-rich but economically-strapped country to tap the government paper market for much-needed cash.
The National (central) Bank said five billion manats' worth of one-month T-Bills were auctioned at an average discount of 7.58 percent, producing an average annualised yield of 31.18 percent.
Investors, mainly newly-authorised dealers, snapped up the entire issue of short-term paper, giving the state coffers 4.87 billion manat in revenue.

The former Soviet republic of Azerbaijan sits on huge oil reserves in its sector of the Caspian Sea and has attracted billions of dollars in foreign investment from Western and Japanese oil consortiums.

But its economy is in shambles after seven years of a debilitating war with Armenia over the disputed Nagorno-Karabakh enclave and economic reforms have lagged behind those in most former Soviet republics.
Gross domestic product shrank 17.2 percent last year after a 21.9 percent slip in 1994, and industrial output showed similarly steep declines.
There is a rudimentary two-tier banking system, with nearly 250 small banks. Parliament has passed a law on securities, but there are no stock exchanges or investment funds.
The country has not undertaken privatisation but plans to turn some monopolies into joint-stock companies and possibly later invite in foreign investors.
The International Monetary Fund granted Baku an $85 million, 2-1/2 year standby loan in 1995, but has said the country's reforms have been too slow, especially in privatisation.
